newsitem.title: ISRAEL: East Jerusalem Jewish enclave barred pending appeal.
newsitem.headline: East Jerusalem Jewish enclave barred pending appeal.

text.p: Israel's Interior Ministry said on Monday construction on a new Jewish enclave in Arab East Jerusalem could not be launched until an appeal filed against the plan was heard next month.
The appeal was filed on Sunday by two left-wing members of Jerusalem's city council.

"The appeals committee decided the permit cannot be granted until a ruling is made on the appeal," Interior Ministry spokeswoman Tova Ellinson told Reuters, adding the appeal would probably be heard on August 8.
The news last week that Jerusalem's municipality had authorised the project at Ras al-Amoud outraged Palestinians who claim East Jerusalem as the capital of a future state.
Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu has said he is working to block the plan "at this time".

Jerusalem Mayor Ehud Olmert confirmed that U.S. businessman Irving Moskowitz, who purchased the land and received a permit to build about 70 homes for Jews in the 11,000-strong Arab neighbourhood, could not start work until a ruling was made on the appeal.
"If there was an appeal, the appeal needs to be discussed entirely. Until the appeal is discussed, the owner of the permit cannot implement it," he told Israel's army radio.
Moskowitz is a Miami-based Jewish businessman who bankrolls settlement in occupied areas.
